figures.title: Your claims, scored on ciphertext
figures.caption: Bars: the model's probability that a claim resembles CoAID's “fake” class, computed in the clear. Diamonds: the same probability from the encrypted score the server returned (client decrypts, applies the sigmoid). |Δz| = logit difference.

figures.title: What the classifier actually keys on
figures.caption: Exact term weights obtained by pushing the logistic-regression weights back through the scaler and SVD. Many cues are about source and format (fact-check phrasing vs agency article titles), not medical truth.

figures.title: What encryption costs
figures.caption: Left: median time per encrypted claim (encrypt + server dot product + decrypt) by CKKS ring size; the paper uses N = 32,768. Right: encrypted similarity search returning one ciphertext per item (naive) vs all scores packed into one ciphertext.
